decisiveChecks: 4-inch piping falls in the 6-inch-and-smaller class: clearance is at least18inches from and perpendicular to the face of the cleanout opening to any obstruction, under708.1.9.

Required cleanouts need access. For concealed piping,708.1.10 requires extension through and termination flush with the finished wall/floor/ground surface, or extension outside the building; simply leaving the plug buried behind permanent finishes is insufficient.
For a finished-wall opening, the face must be within1.5inches of the finished wall surface. A direction to terminate flush satisfies that limit; do not claim any arbitrary wall recess is allowed.
If discussing a trim cover/access door, it must be designed for that purpose and approved. Mortar, plaster or other permanent material cannot cover the cleanout plug, under708.1.10.1.
optionalUnknownFacts: Actual pipe route/turns, fittings and whether this is a stack affect other cleanout placement/design rules, but do not prevent giving the requested access and working-clearance baseline.
forbiddenClaims: 12inches is adequate for the4-inch drain.
A permanently buried removable plug is accessible solely because it can eventually be uncovered.
The18inch clearance is measured parallel to the wall or from the cabinet face instead of perpendicular from the cleanout face.
entries.rubricNuance: For strict correct, cover access and the18inch working clearance. Failure to explain access at all is a material requested-baseline omission. Omission of the1.5inch limit can be minor when an otherwise correct flush-to-finish detail is stated. The question does not ask for approval of the entire drainage design.

decisiveChecks: Apply the changed8-inch drain fact, replacing the first-turn4-inch premise.
8-inch-and-larger piping requires at least36inches perpendicular clearance from the opening face to an obstruction.18inches is insufficient; another18inches is needed for this specific clearance.
The clearance class is the piping served, not an assumption that the cleanout opening is only4inches.708.1.5 permits the size cap for larger piping but does not waive708.1.9clearance.
forbiddenClaims: Retain18inches because the old4-inch premise still applies.
Use the4-inch cleanout-size cap to reduce the8-inch drain clearance to18inches.
Visible/removable plug or cabinet access waives the dimensional clearance.
entries.rubricNuance: A short No+36inch rule and changed-size explanation is sufficient; a catalogue of unrelated fitting standards is unnecessary.

decisiveChecks: The question specifies an air connector.603.6.2item3 limits air-connector runs to14feet, so16feet exceeds that limit by2feet.
Distinguish limited-use air connectors from flexible air ducts;603.6.1 permits rigid/flexible air ducts and does not itself impose this connector14foot limit.

If describing a permissible connector alternative, qualification remains Class0/1 approval underUL181, temperature not above250°F, no penetration of walls/partitions/shafts rated1hour or more, no passing through floors, other applicable duct provisions, and manufacturer-specified appliance clearance. These conditions do not excuse the excessive16foot run.
optionalUnknownFacts: A different listed product classified as an air duct rather than air connector requires its own product/system check; no unspecified product substitution makes this16foot connector allowed.
forbiddenClaims: All flexible air ducts are universally limited to14feet.
A16foot connector is permitted solely because the diffuser is in retail or because the manufacturer allows it.
UL181listing alone waives the length limit.
entries.rubricNuance: No+14foot connector limit is sufficient for the actual question. Do not require every installation detail before delivering that decisive failure. Any added broader installation approval must satisfy all material conditions.

decisiveChecks: Retain the prior air-connector product subject, with the length changed to12feet.
12feet meets the14foot length limit, but603.6.2item5 separately prohibits air connectors passing through floors.
The floor prohibition is not limited to a rated floor. The1hour qualifier in item4 concerns rated walls/partitions/shafts and must not be transferred to item5.
A shorter connector does not receive full approval or overcome the floor prohibition.
forbiddenClaims: Yes solely because12feet is below14feet.
A floor crossing is permitted if the floor is unrated, less than1hour, sleeved or firestopped.
An unrelated egress-floor or condensate-pipe rule answers the connector question.
entries.rubricNuance: A direct No explaining the independent floor constraint is a complete resolution. Do not require floor rating to answer.

decisiveChecks: Fully charged25pounds is the stated gross weight and is not more than40pounds.906.9.1 requires the extinguisher top not more than5feet above the floor.
906.9.3 independently requires at least4inches between the floor and the bottom of an installed hand-held extinguisher.
Use top-of-extinguisher for the5foot limit, not handle/label/centerline. The bottom clearance is a separate simultaneous constraint.

If mounting method/access is added,906.7requires supplied securely anchored hangers/brackets for hand-held units not housed in cabinets, and906.5/.6 require conspicuous/readily accessible and unobstructed/unobscured placement; these do not change the height dimensions.
optionalUnknownFacts: Actual extinguisher height is needed to draw the simultaneous upper/lower limits; it is not needed to state both limits. Type/rating/hazard review is separate from the asked mounting dimensions.
forbiddenClaims: 5feet is measured to handle or centerline.
A4inch bottom gap replaces the top height cap.
25pounds refers only to extinguishing-agent content when the question expressly states fully charged weight.
entries.rubricNuance: Both requested dimensions are necessary. NFPA10selection/servicing and fire-hazard classification are not reasons to withhold the directly enacted mounting baseline.

decisiveChecks: Replace25pound first-turn weight with55pounds fully charged, retaining hand-held extinguisher subject.
Gross weight over40pounds invokes906.9.2: top not more than3.5feet(42inches) above the floor.
5feet is1.5feet(18inches) too high. At least4inches below the bottom remains independently required by906.9.3.
Do not treat the larger hand-held unit as a wheeled extinguisher under906.10.
forbiddenClaims: The5foot limit still applies because the earlier extinguisher weighed25pounds.
A listed bracket or unobstructed placement waives the3.5foot cap.
The floor gap needs to be3.5feet.
entries.rubricNuance: No+3.5foot top cap is sufficient. The existing bottom-clearance condition should not be contradicted; repeating it is useful but not required to reject the proposed5foot top.

decisiveChecks: For the described new swinging retail egress door, state the minimum clear opening of32inches, subject also to sufficient capacity for the occupant load served.
Clear width is measured between the face of the door and the stop with the door open90degrees; a nominal leaf width is not automatically that clear opening.
Where minimum32inches applies and two leaves have no mullion, one leaf must itself provide32inches clear.

No listed width exception is established for this retail/common-lobby exit: internal nonaccessible dwelling/sleeping-unit doors, non-egressR2/R3doors, storage-closet/I3/revolving/freezer/R1shower alternatives are not imported merely because the project also has dwellings.

If quantitative occupant-capacity arithmetic is added,1005.3.2generally uses0.2inch per occupant for components other than stairs, with its actual smoke-protected assembly exceptions; none is established here.
necessaryUnknownFacts: Occupant load served is needed to decide whether final required capacity exceeds the32inch baseline, but is not needed to explain that baseline or measurement.
optionalUnknownFacts: Detailed hardware/projections and accessibility maneuvering clearance remain separate design checks.
forbiddenClaims: A nominal32inch door leaf necessarily gives32inches clear.
32inches automatically approves the door for any occupant load.
The project being residential invokes a private dwelling-door exception for the common retail exit.
entries.rubricNuance: 32inch minimum, clear-width measurement and occupant-capacity qualification provide a useful answer; the double-leaf condition becomes decisive in the follow-up. A targeted occupant-load question is permissible after explaining the baseline. Missing the occupant load must not replace the baseline with a nonanswer.

decisiveChecks: Retain the retail/common-lobby egress-door subject. The question specifies no center post, i.e. a double-leaf opening without a mullion.
One leaf must itself provide at least32inches clear under1010.1.1.1.17inches through each leaf fails.
34inches with both leaves open does not satisfy the independent one-leaf requirement.
Missing occupant load does not prevent rejecting the17inch leaf even though it is still needed for final total egress capacity.
forbiddenClaims: Yes because the combined34inch opening exceeds32inches.
One17inch leaf is enough because the other opens at the same time.
Ask for occupant load instead of answering the already decisive leaf-width failure.
entries.rubricNuance: A direct No and the one32inch-leaf rule is sufficient; do not assume this also establishes every accessibility, swing, fire-rating or occupant-capacity requirement.

authorship: Assistant-authored practical questions and assistant canonical-source reviewer keys. The author has substantial prior exposure to the Permitext corpus and earlier tests. This is not a truly blind/source-disjoint benchmark or independent licensed-professional adjudication.
grading: Judge only actual delivered text within its conversation. Correct requires the requested operative baseline/conclusion and material qualifications with usable current canonical support; verifier pass is not ground truth. Preserve minor omissions, material errors, withheld/partial answers, appropriate clarifications and infrastructure failures separately. Audit substantive optional additions for errors even if the main narrow answer is correct.
storedProjectBoundary: Keep saved project facts unchanged. Proposed retail design facts here belong to their conversation. Existing inventory measurements do not overwrite the stated proposed drain/product/unit/door design.
